name: Singapore Management University
description: Singapore Management University is a publicly funded university established in 2000, with a city campus in Singapore's Bras Basah district. It specialises in business, economics, accountancy, law, computing and the social sciences, taught in a seminar-style format.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded Autonomous Universities, and the local reference point for business, economics and law degrees that Singaporean students often compare with overseas alternatives.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Business Management
programmes.notes: Annual tuition for AY2026/27 entering freshmen from SMU's official 'Tuition Fees & Grant' page, fixed for the normal 4-year candidature (one rate for all non-Law degrees). Citizen S$11,550 (Tier A Tuition Grant) and PR S$16,100 (Tier B), both excl. GST (GST subsidised by the Government). International S$26,200 = Tier C Tuition Grant rate for non-ASEAN students, incl. 9% GST (ASEAN S$25,150; non-subsidised S$47,700). Compulsory fees = 2026 annual miscellaneous student fees: S$281 (SC/PR) or S$367 (international), charged each Term 1. admissions.smu.edu.sg blocks bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-09-30, hence sourceType secondary. The page shows only the AY2026/27 cohort; no earlier years' figures are published there.

programmes.name: Master of Science in Financial Economics (MSFE)
programmes.notes: Self-funded programme: one tuition fee for all nationalities, no MOE-subsidised Citizen/PR rate. Official School of Economics MSFE page, 'Programme Fees' table: 'Tuition Fee for January 2027 Intake' S$54,500 inclusive of GST for the whole programme (billed S$21,800 + S$16,350 + S$16,350), with no separate SC/PR column, so the same tuition is recorded under citizen, pr and international; divided here by the 18-month full-time duration (flexible to 12 months). feeYear 2026 covers the January 2027 (AY2026/27) intake. The only Citizen/PR difference the page publishes is the one-off non-refundable registration fee on acceptance: S$400 incl. GST for Singapore Citizens/PRs, S$500 for international students; the S$5,000 deposit contributes to tuition and is not counted separately. MOE check (2026-10-01): MOE's Tuition Grant Scheme page (moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/tuition-grant-scheme, updated 23 Jun 2026) covers 'selected full-time diploma and undergraduate courses' only; MOE parliamentary replies of 10 Jan 2023 and 24 Sep 2025 state that only around 20% of master's-by-coursework programmes at the autonomous universities are MOE-subsidised (profession-entry or sector-agency-aligned programmes) and the rest are non-subsidised; SMU's own list of MOE-subsidised graduate programmes (graduatestudies.smu.edu.sg/research-masters/programme-fees) contains only MPhil programmes, not the MSFE. The MSFE page's 'Discounts' section lists only a 10% SMU/SUTD alumni discount and says SMU may amend discount schemes per cohort. SMU's central 25th-anniversary scheme (media release 29 Oct 2024, 'from January 2025 onwards') advertises a S$5,000 discount for Singapore Citizens/PRs on the base fee before GST, not combinable with other discounts, but the MSFE programme page does not list it, its alumni discount differs from the central scheme, and SMU's discount calculator says discounts 'may vary depending on the specific programme', so no SC/PR net fee is derived here; a citizen or PR should ask SMU whether that discount applies to the MSFE. The page states the August 2027 intake fee rises to S$57,700 incl. GST (also shown on masters.smu.edu.sg/msfe as 'from August 2027 intake onwards') and that from AY2027 an annual miscellaneous fee of S$400 (SC/PR) or S$480 (international), excl. GST, replaces the registration fee. SMU's sites block bots, so the official pages were read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. No earlier intake's fee is published.

programmes.name: Master of Science in Applied Finance (MAF)
programmes.notes: Self-funded programme (no MOE subsidy; the page publishes no separate SC/PR rate). Official Lee Kong Chian School of Business MAF page: tuition fee S$63,220 inclusive of GST for the whole programme, one figure for all nationalities, so the same tuition is recorded under citizen, pr and international; divided here by the 18-month full-time duration (24 months part-time). The only intake shown is August 2027 (applications September 2026 to May 2027), hence feeYear 2027; the page says the August 2027 fees are indicative and subject to revision. Compulsory fees = annual Miscellaneous Fees for AY2027: S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$480 (international), excl. GST. The S$8,000 advance tuition fee contributes to the first tuition billing and is not counted separately; application fee S$100 excluded. SMU's sites block bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. No earlier intake's fee is published.

programmes.name: Master of IT in Business (MITB)
programmes.notes: Self-funded programme (no MOE subsidy; the page publishes no separate SC/PR rate). Official SMU MITB page, 'Programme Fees' section: total tuition S$56,680 inclusive of 9% GST for the whole programme, one figure for all nationalities, so the same tuition is recorded under citizen, pr and international. Full-time duration is 12 months (payment schedule 'Full-time (1 year)'; a 16-month full-time and a 24-month part-time option exist), so the whole-programme fee equals the annual figure. The payment schedule shows the same S$56,680 for both the January 2027 and August 2027 intakes; feeYear 2026 covers the January 2027 (AY2026/27) intake, and the page says the August 2027 figures are indicative. One-off fee = non-refundable registration fee: S$400 (Singapore Citizens/PRs) or S$500 (foreigners); from the August 2027 intake it is replaced by an annual miscellaneous fee of S$400 (SC/PR) or S$480 (foreigners), excl. GST. The S$10,000 deposit (S$8,000 from August 2027) forms part of the tuition fee and is not counted separately; application fee S$100 and textbooks excluded. SMU's sites block bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. No earlier intake's fee is published.

programmes.name: Juris Doctor (JD)
programmes.notes: Self-funded graduate-entry law degree (no MOE Tuition Grant). Official Yong Pung How School of Law page 'Finance & Administrative Matters for JD Programme, Admit Year 2026': tuition fee for the entire programme S$81,750 incl. GST, the same for all nationalities, billed in four instalments over the first two years (S$5,000 advance deposit + S$15,437.50 + 3 x S$20,437.50); divided here by the 3-year full-time candidature. One-off fee = non-refundable registration fee on offer acceptance: S$400 for Singaporeans/PRs, S$500 for international students. Textbooks and course materials are extra. law.smu.edu.sg blocks bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-09-30, hence sourceType secondary. Only the 2026 admit year is published.

programmes.name: Master of Laws (LLM)
programmes.notes: Self-funded programme (no MOE subsidy). Official SMU LLM 'Fees & Scholarships' page: tuition fee for the August 2027 intake S$39,240 incl. GST for the whole one-year programme (Judicial Studies, Cross-Border Business and Finance Law in Asia, and Law and Technology tracks), the same for all nationalities; the page says the 2027 figure is indicative and subject to revision. It includes a non-refundable S$8,000 tuition deposit, which is not counted separately. Compulsory fees = annual miscellaneous fees from the 2027 intake: S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$480 (foreigners), excl. GST. Application fee S$100 excluded. The Dual LLM (Singapore & London) track costs S$37,605 to SMU plus GBP 22,975 to QMUL. law.smu.edu.sg blocks bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-09-30, hence sourceType secondary. No earlier intake's fee is published on the page.
